newsitem.title: BELGIUM: GUEST COLUMN - BELGIAN MUTUAL FUND ASSOCIATION.
newsitem.headline: GUEST COLUMN - BELGIAN MUTUAL FUND ASSOCIATION.

text.p: Following is a guest column contributed by the Belgian Mutual Fund Association.
Market growth in the third quarter of 1996

The Belgian investment fund industry, defined as publicly offered mutual funds, SICAVs and SICAFs under Belgian and foreign law, grew by 2.9 percent in the third quarter. On September 30 funds and SICAV/Fs totalled 2,173 billion Belgian francs, 60.7 billion francs more than at the end of June.

Total assets of funds investing in fixed-income products (bond, medium-term and money market funds) grew by 35.5 billion francs in the third quarter, resulting in a market share of 65 percent on September 30.

Whereas net assets of bond funds grew by 4.6 percent, those of the medium-term funds and the money market funds decreased by a respective 12.1 and 1.6 percent as redemptions slightly exceeded the sales.
Funds investing in non-fixed income products (equity, guaranteed index, mixed, pension and real-estate funds) rose by 25.2 billion francs and now account for 35 percent of the market.
The growth of net assets of the equity funds (+ 1.3 percent), pension funds (+ 2.8 percent) and mixed funds (+ 3.1 percent) was due to higher share prices rather than new net sales.
Looking more closely at the favourable development of the market in the third quarter, it may be observed that newly launched funds witnessed an important inflow of new capital:
- 8 newly launched (compartments of) guaranteed index funds resulted in a net placement of 7.1 billion francs in the quarter.
- 22 newly launched (compartments of) bond, equity, mixed and money market funds resulted in a net placement of 20 billion francs in the third quarter.
The share of funds under foreign law (most of all Luxembourg schemes) distributed in Belgium was 1,327.1 billion francs, i.e. 61.1 percent of the market.
